scorer_penalty.rationale: kelvin_pairs_gate_fail=2 (both cable 1 and cable 2 have failing Kelvin nets in failing_reasons) while kelvin_unrouted=1 due to the metric's boolean-per-pair undercount. Raising the per-unit weight from 1000 to 2000 partially compensates for the structural undercount: when kelvin_unrouted correctly reports 1 for a true single-cable failure the penalty is proportionate; when it undercounts a two-cable failure (as here), the doubled weight narrows the gap between reported and true cost. This increases candidate-selection pressure toward zero-Kelvin-failure candidates without requiring a metric redefinition.

Before either stage runs, the manager MUST extract the complete set of /SENSEC*_HI and /SENSEC*_LO net names plus all nets currently in kelvin_stub_priority and register them as an exclusion list passed directly into each stage as an initialization argument. No stub whose origin net appears in this exclusion list may be classified as an orphan or spur and removed, regardless of geometric properties (dangling endpoint, zero-length, disconnected from any pad, or any other heuristic). If any net in kelvin_stub_priority has ALL of its stubs removed by orphan-removal or spur-trimming, the manager MUST immediately log 'orphan_or_spur_kelvin_removal_detected' recording: (a) the round number, (b) which nets lost all stubs, (c) whether each loss was classified as orphan or spur, and (d) the geometric property that triggered the classification. The FR dispatch MUST be aborted immediately after this log, before the absorber stage runs. This rule fires earlier in the pipeline than Rule 11's absorber_kelvin_purge_detected check: Rule 11 remains in force as the mandatory backstop, but the absorber should never become the first-line defense for Kelvin stub loss that originates in pre-absorber stages. The current round (round 24) is the reference case: removed_orphans=2, trimmed_spurs=2, absorbed=3, zero Kelvin nets in final output — the pre-absorber stages are the suspected first point of loss.
